crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Board Advisory and Fiduciary Risk
children.blurb: This page covers the fiduciary duties of corporate directors when their companies adopt or rely on artificial intelligence, including the duty of care, the duty of loyalty, and the obligation to oversee material risks.

children.name: Supply Chain and Sustainability Auditing
children.blurb: Supply chain and sustainability auditing uses AI to verify environmental, social, and governance claims across tiers of suppliers, logistics, and product lifecycles.

children.name: Insider Trading and Market Abuse Detection
children.blurb: Insider trading and market abuse detection covers surveillance of trading activity, communications, and employee conduct to identify suspicious patterns that may indicate misuse of material non-public information or market manipulation.

children.name: Regulatory Change Mapping
children.blurb: Regulatory change mapping is the practice of identifying, tracking, and interpreting changes in laws, rules, guidance, and enforcement priorities that affect an organization's use of AI and its governance obligations.

children.name: Merger and Restructuring Analysis
children.blurb: This page covers the use of AI to support legal and compliance work in mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, and corporate restructurings.

sections.body: Corporate governance and regulatory compliance is the work of helping boards, compliance teams, and deal teams understand and manage the rules that apply to AI systems and the companies that use them. In practice, AI is used to scan large volumes of policy documents, regulatory updates, contracts, and internal communications, then flag changes, gaps, and patterns that humans might miss. Board advisory work uses AI to summarize fiduciary duties, risk registers, and oversight questions, while supply chain and sustainability auditing uses AI to trace suppliers, check certifications, and compare ESG disclosures against evidence. Insider trading and market abuse detection uses AI to monitor trading patterns, communications, and market data for anomalies. Regulatory change mapping uses AI to track new bills, rules, and guidance across jurisdictions and connect them to specific business processes. Merger and restructuring analysis uses AI to model combinations, divestitures, and integration risks against regulatory constraints.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field is partly solved and partly unsettled. Document review, regulatory tracking, and anomaly detection are mature enough to be useful, but they still produce false positives and require human review. The site tracks 146 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, and 29 AI case law precedents, which shows that legal standards are still forming. There are 215 compliance and regulation pages and 6940 state AI bills, a volume that no manual process can fully absorb. What is not solved is causation, intent, and accountability when an AI system contributes to a governance failure, and boards still need to decide how much to rely on AI outputs. The honest limit is that AI can map rules and surface risk, but it cannot make a fiduciary judgment or guarantee compliance.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section fit together as a sequence from oversight to transaction, and a reader would go to each for a different layer of the same problem. Board Advisory and Fiduciary Risk is the starting point for directors who need to understand their duties and how AI affects oversight. Supply Chain and Sustainability Auditing goes outward to suppliers, ESG claims, and operational evidence. Insider Trading and Market Abuse Detection focuses on markets, communications, and surveillance. Regulatory Change Mapping connects all of these to the shifting patchwork of rules and bills. Merger and Restructuring Analysis brings the section into deal work, where governance, compliance, supply chain, and market conduct all meet.
